newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower led by silver.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower led by silver.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended lower Wednesday, on moderate volumes, led by further weakness in silver which fell to new six week lows on fund selling late in the day, traders said.

"Funds have been net long silver for some time, but May silver continued to weaken technically this week, falling back below the popular 50-day moving average, but open interest is rising, suggesting more than just fund liquidation of long positions may be going on," Refco New York metals analyst, Tim Porter, said.
COMEX May silver ended down 13.5 cents at $4.870 an ounce, after slipping to a session low at $4.860, its lowest level since February 11.
Standard daily momentum oscillators remained negative, but are not far from oversold levels, and support in the contract was now seen around $4.850, analysts said.
Funds had been net long in COMEX silver, NYMEX platinum and NYMEX palladium, but net short in COMEX gold, according to the latest CFTC data on March 25.
But open interest in COMEX silver has been rising and jumped a further 2,602 lots Tuesday to 93,926 contracts.
Silver was weaker than gold Wednesday, pushing up the spot gold/silver ratio rose further Wednesday to 71.6, as it continues its recovery from 22-month lows around 65.6 on February 14.
COMEX June gold ended down $2.60 at $352.20, but is still holding above support around $350.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $348.80/30, compared to the London afternoon fix Wednesday at $351.05, and Tuesday's New York close around $351.70/20.

"Overall though the precious metals complex still looks to be consolidating the gains made earlier this year, helped perhaps by a weakening equities market," said Andre Dimino, New Jersey based fund manager with Apostle Capital Management.
U.S. bond yields were little changed Wednesday, but stocks market values continued to slide, following last week's monetary policy tightening by the U.S. Federal Reserve.
"If (U.S. Federal Reserve chairman) Greenspan thinks inflation is rising, you would think gold prices would rise," said Hans Kashyap, president of Analytics Research Corp of Maryland.
"But gold is not much of an inflation hedge anymore, only perhaps a catastrophe hedge.
"Nevertheless, the longer the overall sideways move in gold of the last few week's goes on, the more there is a chance of a move to the upside on a break above $355.00 basis June," he said.

NYMEX July platinum closed down $4.50 at $371.80 an ounce, while NYMEX June palladium lost $3.90 to $147.50, but both the platinum group metals have found support in the past week not far below Wednesday's levels.
Disruptions to Russian supplies, concern about the low level of Russian stockpiles, and rising auto demand for PGMs remain the focus for the PGM market, analysts said.
